title: Finite rational functions acquire roots under polynomial substitution
statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R[X])$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of prime characteristic $p$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], and let $n,m\geq0$ and $a_i\in F$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. There exists a finite field extension $E/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with compatible $R$-algebra structure. Put $A=\operatorname{integralClosure}_R(E)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. There is a field embedding $h:F\to\operatorname{Frac}(A[T])$ whose restriction to $R[X]$ is the coefficient map $R\to A$ and substitution $X\mapsto T^{p^n}$, and for each $i$ an element $z_i\in\operatorname{Frac}(A[T])$ with $z_i^{p^n}=h(a_i)$. Every field is in the universe of $R$. No normality, Noetherian or Japanese hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032O, coefficient-root construction in the second assertion (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O); omitted finite-coefficient details expanded in the Lean proof

proof.text: Use IsFractionRing.div_surjective to present the finitely many a_i as quotients of polynomials P_i/D_i over R. Take the finite union S of their nonzero coefficients. In an algebraic closure Ω of K=Frac(R), choose p^n-th roots rt(r) of the images of r in S. Adjoin their finite image to K to form the actual subfield E. Every generator is integral over K since its positive p^n-th power is in K (IsIntegral.of_pow). IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin gives E/K finite.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032O, coefficient-root construction in the second assertion (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O); omitted finite-coefficient details expanded in the Lean proof

proof.text: Equip E with the R-algebra structure through K. Each rt(r) is integral over R, again by IsIntegral.of_pow because its power is the image of r. Thus it gives an element of A=integralClosure R E with the same power equation. The coefficient map R→A is injective, as follows by composing with A→E and the injective maps R→K→E.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032O, coefficient-root construction in the second assertion (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O); omitted finite-coefficient details expanded in the Lean proof

proof.text: Define j:R[X]→A[T] by coefficient mapping and X↦T^(p^n). This equals polynomial map followed by Polynomial.expand; both are injective, the latter by positivity of p^n. Compose with A[T]→Frac(A[T]) and extend to F using IsFractionRing.lift. Its algebraMap compatibility gives precisely the required substitution formula.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032O, coefficient-root construction in the second assertion (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O); omitted finite-coefficient details expanded in the Lean proof

proof.text: For each P_i and D_i, the coefficient-root equations show its mapped polynomial belongs to the image of Polynomial.mapRingHom(iterateFrobenius A p n), by Polynomial.mem_map_range. Choose its preimage Q_i or B_i. Polynomial.map_iterateFrobenius_expand and Polynomial.map_expand imply Q_i^(p^n)=j(P_i) and B_i^(p^n)=j(D_i). Their quotient in Frac(A[T]) has p^n-th power h(a_i), using div_pow, map_pow and map_div₀. The rooted denominator is nonzero because its power is the injective image of the original denominator. Zero numerators, n=0 and m=0 all fit the same proof.

from.place: Finite coefficient-root construction in the positive-characteristic normalization argument, refined to a finite family of fractions; step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-polynomial-cover

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_fraction_root_substitution
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) p]
    (n m : ℕ) (a : Fin m → FractionRing (Polynomial R)) :
    ∃ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E) (_ : Algebra (FractionRing R) E) (_ : Algebra R E)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R (FractionRing R) E) (_ : FiniteDimensional (FractionRing R) E),
      ∃ h : FractionRing (Polynomial R) →+* FractionRing (Polynomial (integralClosure R E)),
        (∀ b : Polynomial R,
          h (algebraMap (Polynomial R) (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) b) =
            algebraMap (Polynomial (integralClosure R E))
              (FractionRing (Polynomial (integralClosure R E)))
              (Polynomial.eval₂RingHom
                (Polynomial.C.comp (algebraMap R (integralClosure R E)))
                (Polynomial.X ^ (p ^ n)) b)) ∧
        ∀ i, ∃ z : FractionRing (Polynomial (integralClosure R E)), z ^ (p ^ n) = h (a i)
